task.description: Read docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-001b.md independently. Run WF-02 Step 3b's gate: (a) every one of REQ-001b's 5 acceptance criteria has at least one verification case; (b) no TODO left; (c) every case is precise enough to run without judgment (exact command, exact expected output). Since the spec covers a 177-key surface with only 6 checks, specifically assess whether that coverage is genuinely adequate (does it actually exercise all 12 components, not just 3 spot-checks that happen to pass?) or whether it under-covers by sampling too thin a slice. Re-run at least 2 of the spec's own commands yourself to confirm they produce the exact output the spec claims.
acceptance_criteria: Checks a-c run against docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-001b.md directly
A judgment made on whether 6 checks genuinely cover all 12 components adequately, or whether gaps exist
At least 2 commands from the spec re-run independently with matching output confirmed

result.summary: Read docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-001b.md independently and ran WF-02 Step 3b's gate. (a) All 5 acceptance criteria have at least one verification case: AC1 (Cyrillic sweep + getTranslations companion check), AC2 (key-set diff), AC3 (empty-value check), AC4 (build check), AC5 (four sub-parts 5a-5d covering error-marker sweep, 3 spot checks across the 3 extraction patterns, t.rich() escaping check, and section-presence/count checks). (b) No 'TODO' found (grep returned zero matches). (c) Every case specifies an exact command and exact expected output/exit code with no judgment required. Coverage-adequacy assessment: the 6 check-families are non-redundant and jointly target distinct, realistic failure classes for a 177-key/12-component surface -- AC1+AC2 alone give structural guarantees (no leftover Cyrillic, no deleted-not-extracted components, no missing/extra/empty keys) but not semantic/runtime correctness; that gap is closed by AC5's layered checks (5a catches broken runtime resolution via MISSING_MESSAGE/IntlError markers, 5c catches t.rich() HTML-escaping specifically, 5d's section-count catches a silently-aborted Server Component section that neither the Cyrillic sweep nor the key-diff could see). The 3 spot checks correctly sample by extraction-mechanism risk (flat key, indexed/repeated-shape array, Footer literal) rather than by string count, which is the right axis since a bug is far more likely to be systematic to a mechanism than isolated to one arbitrary string. One narrow residual gap accepted as reasonable at this scale: a correct, non-empty value pasted under the wrong (but structurally valid) key among the ~170 non-spot-checked keys would not be caught by any of the 6 checks. Independently re-ran 4 of the spec's own commands (AC1 Cyrillic sweep, AC1 getTranslations companion, AC2 key-set diff, AC3 empty-value check) -- all 4 outputs matched the spec's claimed output exactly: files_scanned 12/cyrillic_matches [], getTranslations count 12, ru_count/uz_count 177/177 with key_sets_match true and empty diffs, uz_keys_total 177 with empty_uz_values []. No check failures. Gate PASSES.
